transition_or_process: Postharvest vegetative growth to next-season reproductive potential
cause_or_driver: Shoot growth cessation; photoperiod; temperature; cultivar; canopy health
biological_state_change: Vegetative shoots transition to reproductive bud initiation and differentiation
yield_or_timing_consequence: Sets a portion of next-season flower potential
evidence_synthesis: Short days and temperature affect flower initiation in tested cultivars; initiation timing can overlap harvest or occur later
limitations_or_conflicts: Type and cultivar alter timing; calendar date is not portable
contract_note: Represent prior-season shoot and flower-bud potential as cross-season state with unknown cultivar parameters

transition_or_process: Shoot and canopy traits to flower-bud number
cause_or_driver: Productive shoot density; cane age; light; crop load; pruning
biological_state_change: Changes available nodes and the probability/number of reproductive buds
yield_or_timing_consequence: Changes potential bloom and fruit set
evidence_synthesis: Field and developmental studies show bud counts and initiation vary by shoot/cane context
limitations_or_conflicts: Observational associations do not give one universal bud-per-shoot coefficient
contract_note: Separate structural shoot state from reproductive bud state

transition_or_process: Photoperiod and temperature to floral induction
cause_or_driver: Short-day exposure and temperature regime
biological_state_change: Inductive floral transition in susceptible genotypes
yield_or_timing_consequence: Changes future flowering potential
evidence_synthesis: Controlled studies support photoperiod and temperature effects in highbush materials
limitations_or_conflicts: Thresholds depend on genotype and protocol
contract_note: Represent environmental cues and cultivar-specific response parameters; do not freeze a universal threshold

transition_or_process: Pruning to structure and reproductive sink
cause_or_driver: Pruning time; type; intensity; removed fruiting wood
biological_state_change: Changes cane-age structure; fruiting wood; bud load; canopy and potential leaf area
yield_or_timing_consequence: Can alter crop load; berry traits; harvest timing; next-year bud potential
evidence_synthesis: Field trials show severity and load effects on yield and berry size/quality
limitations_or_conflicts: Season, site, cultivar, and pruning definition modify effects
contract_note: Model as a timed scoped event with affected structure and sink; no single pruning multiplier

transition_or_process: Pruning timing-specific cross-year effect
cause_or_driver: Postharvest versus summer versus dormant pruning
biological_state_change: May alter shoot regrowth, flower-bud induction, reserves, and canopy light differently
yield_or_timing_consequence: Potential current- and next-season yield/timing effects
evidence_synthesis: Evidence exists for selected interventions but does not establish a globally transferable effect ordering across all pruning windows
limitations_or_conflicts: Direct matched timing trials across systems are sparse
contract_note: S1 may encode event types; causal parameter values and timing effects remain unresolved

transition_or_process: Flower-bud removal versus pruning
cause_or_driver: Reproductive bud removal without equivalent cane removal
biological_state_change: Reduces reproductive sink while leaving more vegetative structure than branch pruning
yield_or_timing_consequence: Can increase leaf area per fruit and berry size while reducing potential fruit number
evidence_synthesis: Bud-density experiments document load and canopy consequences; winter pruning also removes structure
limitations_or_conflicts: Experiments are not a perfect head-to-head decomposition of every intervention
contract_note: Keep flower-bud thinning/removal separate from pruning

transition_or_process: Flower or fruit thinning to crop load and berry traits
cause_or_driver: Flower-bud load; flower removal; fruitlet or fruit thinning
biological_state_change: Changes effective flower number; fruit number; source per fruit
yield_or_timing_consequence: May trade total yield against berry size, quality, and timing
evidence_synthesis: Manipulation studies show reproductive load affects fruit and vegetative traits
limitations_or_conflicts: Optimal commercial intervention and response curve remain system-specific
contract_note: Track removed and retained reproductive units plus resulting fruit set

transition_or_process: Leaf source availability to fruit growth
cause_or_driver: Leaf area per fruit; leaf health; radiation; water and nutrient supply
biological_state_change: Changes assimilate availability relative to fruit sinks
yield_or_timing_consequence: Can affect berry size, weight, fruit retention and development
evidence_synthesis: Blueberry field work links source-to-sink conditions with fruit and leaf traits
limitations_or_conflicts: Proxy choice and response shape not standardized across cultivars
contract_note: Include source and sink state concepts; calibrate measures before use

transition_or_process: Source-sink ratio as a dynamic numerical law
cause_or_driver: Photosynthesis, stored reserves, fruit/flower load, shoot and root demand
biological_state_change: A scalar ratio is an abstraction over several changing pools and flows
yield_or_timing_consequence: Could modulate retention, berry growth and future bud potential
evidence_synthesis: The source-sink concept is biologically useful but observed studies do not supply one universal dynamic equation
limitations_or_conflicts: Stocks, fluxes and proxies are not interchangeable
contract_note: Do not equate leaf-area-to-fruit ratio with whole-plant carbon balance

transition_or_process: Cold exposure versus dormancy state
cause_or_driver: Temperature history plus intrinsic bud physiology
biological_state_change: Dormancy status may progress independently from a simple cumulative-hour counter
yield_or_timing_consequence: Budbreak competence cannot be inferred from temperature sum alone
evidence_synthesis: Chilling models predict exposure; bud assays and physiological markers show state interpretation is more complex
limitations_or_conflicts: Model outputs do not directly observe endodormancy release
contract_note: Keep chill accumulator and dormancy state as separate variables

transition_or_process: Choice among Chill Hours Utah and Dynamic chill models
cause_or_driver: Hourly temperature response and model assumptions
biological_state_change: Produces different chill accumulation histories
yield_or_timing_consequence: May change estimated dormancy completion date
evidence_synthesis: Models have different response weights and warm-temperature handling; blueberry validation is cultivar- and region-limited
limitations_or_conflicts: No globally validated model selection result for the target production population
contract_note: Record candidate model and source; do not select a production default in S0

transition_or_process: Cultivar-specific chilling requirement
cause_or_driver: Blueberry type; cultivar; bud type; prior environment
biological_state_change: Changes timing and uniformity of dormancy release
yield_or_timing_consequence: Affects budbreak, flowering and exposure to frost
evidence_synthesis: Across blueberry types and cultivars chill responses differ
limitations_or_conflicts: Published thresholds depend on model, bud assay and environment
contract_note: Chill requirement must be cultivar/bud scoped and have explicit authority provenance

transition_or_process: Chilling satisfaction followed by forcing
cause_or_driver: Dormancy status and subsequent effective heat accumulation
biological_state_change: Bud development proceeds toward bud swell, budbreak and bloom
yield_or_timing_consequence: Changes flowering timing and potentially synchrony
evidence_synthesis: Evidence supports sequential chill and warm forcing logic in deciduous systems
limitations_or_conflicts: Forcing response and chill sufficiency vary across cultivars and interventions
contract_note: Represent chill status and forcing accumulation separately

transition_or_process: Chemical dormancy treatment versus thermal forcing
cause_or_driver: Hydrogen cyanamide or defoliant treatment; timing and dose
biological_state_change: Can alter budbreak and phytohormone responses through intervention-specific pathways
yield_or_timing_consequence: May advance budbreak/ripening and may cause flower mortality or yield changes
evidence_synthesis: Treatment studies show effects are not identical to greenhouse heating
limitations_or_conflicts: Specific product, dose, timing, cultivar and safety authority required
contract_note: Encode chemical intervention as a distinct event; no dose/default parameter in S0

transition_or_process: Evergreen or non-dormant production pathway
cause_or_driver: Leaf retention, warm winter, genotype and management
biological_state_change: Can maintain canopy and reproductive activity with reduced or altered dormancy
yield_or_timing_consequence: Can support off-season/early harvest but changes annual state sequence
evidence_synthesis: Florida system evidence distinguishes evergreen/non-dormant production from conventional deciduous cycles
limitations_or_conflicts: Commercial labels and everbearing genetic phenotypes are not synonymous
contract_note: Use separate production-system pathway and explicit leaf-retention state

transition_or_process: Evergreen does not mean zero chilling requirement
cause_or_driver: Leaf-retention system label alone
biological_state_change: Dormancy/chill may be absent, reduced, bypassed, or cultivar-specific
yield_or_timing_consequence: Incorrect zeroing could misstate bloom and harvest timing
evidence_synthesis: A single everbearing genotype bypassed endodormancy under tested conditions; this does not establish a zero requirement for all evergreen systems
limitations_or_conflicts: Need cultivar- and system-specific state evidence
contract_note: Never encode evergreen chill requirement as universal zero

transition_or_process: Pollination and fertilization to fruit set
cause_or_driver: Flower receptivity, compatible pollen, pollinator visits and weather
biological_state_change: Effective fertilization and seed development support fruit set
yield_or_timing_consequence: Changes fruit number and potentially berry growth and maturity
evidence_synthesis: Field and pollination studies show visitation and compatibility influence fruit outcomes
limitations_or_conflicts: Pollinator count is not equal to fertilization or set
contract_note: Separate bloom, effective pollination, fertilization and fruit-set states

transition_or_process: Seed development to berry weight and ripening
cause_or_driver: Pollen source, compatibility, seed number and seed weight
biological_state_change: Alters developing fruit growth signals and resource demand
yield_or_timing_consequence: May affect berry mass and days to ripe
evidence_synthesis: Highbush experiments link pollination/seed traits with berry mass and timing
limitations_or_conflicts: Seed-mediated effects are not uniform across cultivars and years
contract_note: Keep seed/pollination indicators optional until observable and calibrated

transition_or_process: Bloom cohort to fruit cohort
cause_or_driver: Bloom date and successful fruit set
biological_state_change: Creates fruit cohorts with cohort-specific origin date and load
yield_or_timing_consequence: Provides a biologically traceable origin for later maturity timing
evidence_synthesis: Tagged or stage-sampled flowers/fruits show temporal progression from bloom and fertilization into fruit stages
limitations_or_conflicts: Cohort tracking is a model representation rather than a standard field record
contract_note: Use bloom cohort identity and set estimate as causal lineage

transition_or_process: Thermal development to ripe cohort timing
cause_or_driver: Temperature over developmental stages; cultivar; crop load
biological_state_change: Advances or delays stage progression and color break
yield_or_timing_consequence: Changes daily newly mature fruit timing
evidence_synthesis: Degree-day and protected-environment studies support temperature sensitivity but retain cultivar/site residuals
limitations_or_conflicts: No universal base temperature or upper cap validated across all target cultivars
contract_note: Keep thermal response parameters versioned and source-specific

transition_or_process: Three-phase fruit growth
cause_or_driver: Development stage and time after anthesis/fertilization
biological_state_change: Early expansion, lag phase and late expansion/ripening
yield_or_timing_consequence: Changes fruit size and color development trajectory
evidence_synthesis: Multiple anatomical and growth studies support a double-sigmoid organizing pattern
limitations_or_conflicts: Stage nomenclature and physiological interpretation vary
contract_note: Represent stages with definitions and avoid assuming fixed duration

transition_or_process: Protected microclimate to plant state
cause_or_driver: Hourly air/root-zone temperature, radiation, humidity, ventilation and cover
biological_state_change: Changes heat exposure, canopy environment, bud development and fruit conditions
yield_or_timing_consequence: May advance phenology and alter fruit set, yield and quality
evidence_synthesis: Tunnel/greenhouse studies show microclimate and outcomes change together
limitations_or_conflicts: Protection design, ventilation, heating and crop stage differ among studies
contract_note: Represent measured greenhouse microclimate rather than a generic weather offset

transition_or_process: Protected cultivation is not a calendar-date offset
cause_or_driver: Cover closure, heating, freeze protection, radiation and pollinator access
biological_state_change: Changes multiple environmental and biological states
yield_or_timing_consequence: Can change timing and crop amount/quality in different directions
evidence_synthesis: Protected trials report phenology advances alongside cultivar-dependent yield, fruit-set or quality outcomes
limitations_or_conflicts: Results vary across tunnel type and climate
contract_note: Do not reduce protected production to harvest-date subtraction

transition_or_process: Light and CO2 to photosynthetic source capacity
cause_or_driver: Photon flux, CO2, temperature and their interaction
biological_state_change: Changes measured leaf/net photosynthetic response under controlled conditions
yield_or_timing_consequence: Could influence assimilate supply but season-yield linkage is not established by the control study
evidence_synthesis: A greenhouse study measures joint response and optimizes control variables
limitations_or_conflicts: Short measurement window and control objective do not validate whole-season yield effects
contract_note: Treat sensor variables as candidate inputs; avoid mapping controller optimum to crop response default

transition_or_process: Pruning is not a single yield multiplier
cause_or_driver: Event timing, cane removal, bud removal, severity and canopy response
biological_state_change: Changes both source structure and reproductive sink
yield_or_timing_consequence: Can affect current yield, berry traits, ripening and future bud potential
evidence_synthesis: Pruning and flower-bud manipulation studies show multiple pathways and trade-offs
limitations_or_conflicts: Effects depend on what tissue was removed and when
contract_note: Represent intervention components and intensity; never freeze a scalar pruning factor

transition_or_process: Daily newly mature fruit versus harvested fruit
cause_or_driver: Biological ripening, opening mature inventory, losses and picking capacity
biological_state_change: Biological engine produces ripe/mature supply; harvest engine removes available inventory
yield_or_timing_consequence: Separates maturity curve from harvest curve
evidence_synthesis: Fruit maturity biology and harvest operations are distinct observable processes
limitations_or_conflicts: This is a model boundary; literature does not alone specify the existing harvest-state implementation
contract_note: Biological engine output ends at daily newly mature quantity

transition_or_process: Universal staging labels and stage-transition thresholds
cause_or_driver: Anatomical definition, sampling protocol, genotype and observer criteria
biological_state_change: Assigns observed buds/fruits to named states
yield_or_timing_consequence: Affects predicted cohort progression and evaluation comparability
evidence_synthesis: Stage-based evidence exists but stage labels and boundaries are not harmonized across papers
limitations_or_conflicts: Operational staging protocol must be frozen separately
contract_note: S1 should require explicit state definitions and observation rule

transition_or_process: Integrated annual causal graph
cause_or_driver: Prior crop and postharvest state; management; environment; reproductive development
biological_state_change: Links current-season state to next-season buds and current fruit cohorts
yield_or_timing_consequence: Provides a coherent model skeleton for yield and timing
evidence_synthesis: The component mechanisms have evidence but the full end-to-end graph is a synthesis for future model design
limitations_or_conflicts: No single study validates the complete graph quantitatively
contract_note: Use as a candidate contract graph; parameter identifiability remains open

transition_or_process: Early flowering is not equivalent to early commercial harvest
cause_or_driver: Floret count, fruit set, shoot competition and development period
biological_state_change: May change bloom date without producing a larger or earlier harvest
yield_or_timing_consequence: Harvest advancement may fail despite early flowering
evidence_synthesis: Japanese postharvest treatments and tunnel trials show phenology and harvest outcomes can diverge
limitations_or_conflicts: Outcome depends on fruit set, frost, cultivar and crop load
contract_note: Track bloom, set, maturity and harvest separately

transition_or_process: Crop load to next-season bud potential
cause_or_driver: Current reproductive load; postharvest leaf area; reserve status; regrowth
biological_state_change: May affect shoot growth, reserves and later flower-bud formation
yield_or_timing_consequence: Creates a possible biennial/cross-year feedback
evidence_synthesis: Manipulation and field studies support coupling but not a universal carryover coefficient
limitations_or_conflicts: Longitudinal matched data and reserve measures remain limited
contract_note: Represent lagged state and source evidence separately; do not assume a fixed alternate-bearing effect
